scope: Bounded primary-source screen; no GPU, model execution, or data download; official table image downloaded

sources.title: Spatio-Temporal Context Learning with Temporal Difference Convolution for Moving Infrared Small Target Detection
sources.status: published proceedings; official AAAI PDF and author code verified
sources.data_weights: Author README links Google Drive and Baidu Netdisk for weights and IRSTD-UAV; links seen, downloads not tested
sources.data: IRSTD-UAV: 17 real video sequences, 15106 frames; IRDST: real videos

evidence.interpretation: Measured loss as frames become more separated. Cannot isolate egomotion: target displacement and temporal horizon change too.

evidence.fact: IRSTD-UAV divides each sequence into 50-frame segments, shuffles and splits 8:2. This is not a held-out-video evaluation; no empirical inflation claim is made.
Released recipe instructs background alignment before train/test with GIM and background_alignment.py.
Static/very slow test exists: 5 sequences ×50 frames; AP50 96.27, recall97.20. Thus do not claim static targets were ignored.

sources.measured_metrics: P/R/F1/AP50 at box IoU0.5; FPS/parameters/FLOPs; temporal-length, slow/static, and frame-interval ablations
sources.not_measured_in_read_sections: Consecutive miss duration, recovery after corrupted support frames, time to first reliable detection, controlled separation of camera and target motion, held-out-scene generalization for IRSTD-UAV
sources.remaining_problem: After increased temporal separation, detection loses recall despite high ordinary-set scores; identify which support correspondence failures generate sustained missed detections, then remedy them.

sources.title: MIST: A Benchmark and Baseline for Multi-frame Infrared Small Target Detection in Complex Motion
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Image Processing 2026, vol35 pp5196–5211
sources.status: Author README records TIP acceptance 2026-04-27; bibliographic record confirms publication
sources.data_weights: Official README links MIST data and pretrained model weights on Google Drive; downloads not tested
sources.data: Targets generated by synthetic engine and blended into real backgrounds; 78 train/42 test sequences, 11-sequence MIST-Hard; not fully real captured target videos

evidence.fact: MIST-Hard combines SCR<=1, highly irregular trajectories, and speeds>7pixels/frame.

evidence.location: Official benchmark TableII image, visually read
evidence.interpretation: Hard subset is measurably harder even for proposed baseline; cross-column comparisons are not a train-on-one/test-on-another transfer experiment.

sources.not_measured_or_not_verified: Full article inaccessible in bounded search; no claims about absent full-paper evaluations. README/table do not establish recovery behavior or isolated abrupt-motion cause. Hard subset changes contrast and motion together.
sources.remaining_problem: Complex-motion/low-contrast sequences remain less reliable; usable controlled data and released model support diagnostic screening, but real-sequence corroboration is required.

sources.title: Rethinking Evaluation of Infrared Small Target Detection
sources.status: Author arXiv comments and official NeurIPS-hosted slides verified; proceedings landing page not retrieved in bounded search

evidence.fact: Separates target localization and segmentation with hIoU/error taxonomy; cross-dataset evaluation. Main evaluation concentrates on single-frame segmentation methods.
Explicitly evaluates three multi-frame methods; hIoU 0.552/0.546/0.591, target localization IoU 0.683/0.669/0.719. These are not evidence about CHAL/TDCNet failures.

sources.measured_metrics: Mask matching, localization/segmentation errors and cross-dataset transfer; multi-frame aggregate extension
sources.what_metrics_conceal: Inference from metric definitions: framewise pooled scores are unchanged if identical per-frame errors are reordered, hence cannot distinguish isolated misses from one long blind interval. Paper does not itself demonstrate temporal burst failures.
sources.remaining_problem: Reuse established spatial error taxonomy and add event-aligned sequence diagnosis rather than claim a new generic metric.

recommendation.problem_statement: 当帧间运动增大、时序对应关系变差时，现有多帧检测器仍出现明显召回下降；需要查清这些漏检是否在连续视频中形成长时间盲区，以及哪些历史帧开始损害当前帧检测，并据此改进时序信息的使用。
recommendation.status: First clause has direct TDCNet evidence. Consecutive blind intervals and harmful history are diagnostic hypotheses, not established findings.
minimal_diagnostic: Reproduce released clean-frame protocol then stratify natural sequences by target displacement, camera motion, contrast and alignment residual.
Measure miss-run length, reacquisition time and false-alarm duration in addition to original detector metrics.
Compare current frame to the same frame with retained/removed/replaced support frames to diagnose temporal help or harm; avoid declaring a module before evidence.
Use held-out-video real sequences; use MIST-Hard as controlled corroboration and keep synthetic/real conclusions distinct.

limitations: No claim that CHAL/HomoDiff exhibit the same failures.
No single-cause attribution to alignment, abrupt acceleration, or memory contamination from current evidence.
Do not describe separate training/testing on two datasets as cross-dataset generalization.
